requirements.title: ADA Title III: Accessible contact and quote-request forms

criteria: Business is a private entity whose operations affect commerce and fall within one of the 12 categories of public accommodation (42 U.S.C. 12181(7)), or the site is connected to such services.
Website-only coverage is legal-interpretation-dependent by circuit.
business_types: pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)

required_behavior: People with disabilities can perceive, operate and complete contact and quote-request forms with assistive technology on equal terms (auxiliary aids and services; effective communication).
WCAG 2.2 AA criteria for forms pass on every contact/quote form; alternative contact (phone/email) is offered.
Conformance is assessed against the WCAG 2.2 Level A/AA baseline in the website-accessibility register.
requirements.enforcement_exposure: DOJ enforcement and private suits for injunctive relief and attorney fees (42 U.S.C. 12188); in California, an ADA violation is also an Unruh Act violation with statutory damages (see WEB-CA-023).
required_evidence: list of third-party widgets in the flow and their accessibility conformance statements (VPAT/ACR)
requirements.notes: DOJ has adopted no Title III web technical standard; its 2022 web guidance (ada.gov/resources/web-guidance) says businesses may choose how to comply and points to WCAG as helpful. WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA is the de facto benchmark in litigation. The 2024 Title II rule (28 CFR 35.200, WCAG 2.1 AA) binds state/local governments only and does not apply to these sites. Whether a website alone (without a physical place) is a 'place of public accommodation' is split among federal circuits; Pacific Plains Electric serves customers at their premises and both sites sell services to the public. requirements.title: ESIGN consumer consent disclosures before electronic records

criteria: The site or its signing flow provides to a consumer, electronically, information that a statute or regulation requires be provided or made available in writing (e.g., California home improvement contract copies and notices under B&P 7159).
Not triggered by a quote form or by B2B (non-consumer) SaaS contracts alone.
business_types: pacificplainselectric.com where contracts/notices are signed or delivered online
volteira.com only if consumer-facing required written disclosures are delivered electronically
transaction_types: Electronic delivery of legally required consumer disclosures

required_behavior: Before consent, give a clear and conspicuous statement of: the right to receive the record on paper; the right to withdraw consent and any conditions/consequences/fees of withdrawal; whether consent covers only this transaction or categories of records; how to withdraw and how to update contact information; how to obtain a paper copy and any fee.
State the hardware and software requirements to access and retain the electronic records.

Obtain the consumer's affirmative consent electronically in a manner that reasonably demonstrates the consumer can access information in the electronic form that will be used (e.g., opening a PDF in the same format).
Consent screen appears before the signing ceremony, not buried in general terms of use.
requirements.enforcement_exposure: Failure means the electronic record may not satisfy the underlying writing requirement (e.g., B&P 7159 contract copy), risking unenforceability and regulatory discipline.
required_evidence: screenshots of the ESIGN disclosure and consent step
copy of the e-sign vendor's consumer disclosure text
audit trail record showing consent timestamp, IP/user agent and disclosure version
requirements.notes: Browser-observable: the presence and content of the disclosure/consent step. Backend: stored consent record. Federal ESIGN 7001(c) applies to consumer disclosures even where California UETA governs the transaction generally (UETA 1633.3/ESIGN 7002 preemption analysis needed). requirements.title: TCPA PEWC: clear and conspicuous marketing-text disclosure at phone collection

criteria: Site collects a mobile phone number that will receive text messages (SMS/MMS) or calls made with an autodialer (ATDS) or artificial/prerecorded voice.

Marketing (telemarketing/advertising) texts require prior express written consent; purely informational/transactional texts (appointment reminders, arrival notices, receipts) require prior express consent.
business_types: pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)
transaction_types: Phone number collection on quote/booking/contact forms

required_behavior: Where marketing texts/calls will be sent, a disclosure adjacent to the phone field (not only in linked terms) clearly states that by opting in the person authorizes the named seller (e.g., 'Pacific Plains Electric' / 'Volteira') to send marketing text messages/calls using automated technology to the number provided.
Disclosure is legible (size/contrast), visible without scrolling away from the control, and written in plain language.
Marketing consent is separate from consent for transactional/informational messages.
requirements.enforcement_exposure: Private right of action $500 per message, trebled to $1,500 for willful/knowing violations (47 U.S.C. 227(b)(3)); class-action risk.
required_evidence: screenshot of each phone-collection form with the disclosure text
requirements.notes: The FCC 'one-to-one consent' amendment to 64.1200(f)(9) was vacated by the Eleventh Circuit (Insurance Marketing Coalition v. FCC, Jan. 2025) before taking effect; naming the specific seller in the consent remains best practice. Post-Facebook v. Duguid (2021) ATDS scope is narrow, but many SMS platforms and state laws (e.g., Florida/Oklahoma mini-TCPAs) still make PEWC the prudent standard. requirements.title: COPPA applicability determination
requirements.amendment_notes: Amended COPPA Rule published April 22, 2025; effective June 23, 2025; general compliance date April 22, 2026 (per prior knowledge; not verified).

criteria: Applies only if the site is directed to children under 13 (in whole or part) or the operator has actual knowledge it collects personal information from a child under 13.
business_types: pacificplainselectric.com (California electrical contractor, Pacific Plains Electric)
exceptions: General-audience B2B SaaS and home-services sites are ordinarily not child-directed.

required_behavior: Document the determination that neither site is child-directed (subject matter, visuals, language, ads) and that no age-gated child data is knowingly collected.

If COPPA applies: post a compliant children's privacy notice, obtain verifiable parental consent before collection, and meet the amended rule's requirements (separate consent for third-party disclosure, written data retention policy, security program).

requirements.title: Reg Z: triggering terms in financing ads require full disclosures

criteria: Site advertises closed-end consumer credit for personal/household purposes (e.g., 'Finance your panel upgrade for $99/month', 'as low as X% APR', partner financing such as Hearth/GreenSky/Synchrony).
exceptions: Business-purpose credit (B2B SaaS) is outside Regulation Z.

required_behavior: If an ad states any triggering term — the amount or percentage of a down payment, the number of payments or period of repayment, the amount of any payment, or the amount of any finance charge — it also clearly and conspicuously states: the down payment amount or percentage; the terms of repayment (over the full term); and the 'annual percentage rate' (using that term) and whether it may increase after consummation.
Applies to any person advertising the credit, including the contractor, not only the creditor.
required_evidence: screenshots of every financing mention with surrounding disclosures

requirements.title: Reg Z: advertised rates stated as APR; 'actually available' terms

criteria: Site advertises closed-end consumer credit for personal/household purposes (e.g., 'Finance your panel upgrade for $99/month', 'as low as X% APR', partner financing such as Hearth/GreenSky/Synchrony).
exceptions: Business-purpose credit (B2B SaaS) is outside Regulation Z.

required_behavior: Any rate of finance charge is stated as an 'annual percentage rate,' using that term, and if the APR may be increased after consummation the ad states that fact; for credit not secured by a dwelling no other rate is stated, except a simple annual rate or periodic rate applied to an unpaid balance stated in conjunction with, but not more conspicuously than, the APR. Required disclosures are clear and conspicuous (1026.24(b)).
Advertised terms are terms that the creditor actually arranges or will arrange.
